name: merge-commit-only
claim: Merge-commit only: pull requests land on main via merge commits; squash merging and rebase merging are prohibited and disabled in repository settings (2026-07-02) - doubly held, since settings enforce it mechanically and this prescription records why, so the setting cannot later be flipped back as a harmless preference.
rules: Pull requests merge via merge commit only; the squash-merge and rebase-merge methods are disabled in repository settings and stay disabled.
A merge never rewrites the SHAs of the commits it lands: any workflow that would re-address merged commits (squash, rebase-and-merge, history rewriting on the default branch) is out of bounds.

Merge-commit messages are not hand-edited to embed PR descriptions: a PR description is review-time conversation, not record - the record is the graph, the in-repo documents, and the constituent commit messages.
invariants: Every commit: artifact cited in the graph dereferences in a fresh clone of the repository; no citation depends on the host's hidden PR refs.

evidence.detail: Stipulated by the operator during PR #10 review, where the id migration made the dependency concrete: cb:b566 cites its migration commit by SHA and its mint commit carries the first Belief: trailer - a squash or rebase merge of that PR would have orphaned both. Squash and rebase merging disabled in repository settings the same day.

Atomization migration (plans/atomize): claim restated to the norm; enumerable content moved to invariants. Descriptive rationale extracted to atoms cb:b825, cb:b826, now deps. Previous claim: Merge-commit only: pull requests land on main via merge commits; squash merging and rebase merging are prohibited and disabled in repository settings (2026-07-02). Both rewrite merged history to new SHAs, and the graph's provenance machinery dereferences merged SHAs: commit: artifacts cite implementing commits by content address, Belief: trailers bind commits to nodes, and nodes like cb:b566 carry commit: citations whose targets must exist in every fresh clone. A squash or rebase merge leaves the cited SHAs reachable only through the host's hidden PR refs - absent from a clean clone - so mix cb.verify.commits fails and the belief-commit loop is severed. The prohibition is doubly held: repository settings enforce it mechanically, and this prescription records why, so the setting cannot later be flipped back as a harmless preference.
